blocks.text: I can explain how I know that ‘A Midsummer Night’s Dream’ is a comedy.
Tap each word to see what it means.

items.def: the style or type of text: for example science fiction
a play designed to make you laugh, often involving misunderstandings and ending in marriage
physical comedy, sometimes violent but intended to make people laugh
the first collection of most of Shakespeare’s plays, published in 1623 (seven years after his death)

blocks.text: A **genre** is the style or type of text, for example science fiction. Shakespeare’s plays are often sorted by genre.

Laura says: “I haven’t really seen any Shakespeare plays, but I have heard of ‘Romeo and Juliet’. I know it’s meant to be really sad, and ends in the death of both Romeo and Juliet who are young and in love. I think that means it’s a tragedy.”

blocks.label: How did Laura work out the genre?
blocks.text: She used what she knew about the play: it is really sad and it ends in death. A play’s features can tell us its genre.
The first collection of Shakespeare’s plays was published in 1623, seven years after his death. It is commonly known as the **First Folio**.
The First Folio contains 36 of Shakespeare’s plays and divides them into three genres:

blocks.q: How many genres does the First Folio use to divide Shakespeare’s plays?
blocks.why: The First Folio divides the plays into comedies, histories and tragedies: three genres.

blocks.q: Which of these is NOT one of the First Folio’s genres?
blocks.why: Tragicomedy is an extra genre that was added later; it is not one of the First Folio’s three genres.

blocks.text: Tragedies have some common features:

items: They explore complex ideas like power, ambition and jealousy.
They include a hero who dies because of some sort of weakness in themselves.

blocks.text: ‘Romeo and Juliet’ is an example of a tragedy.

blocks.label: Laura’s view of tragedy
blocks.text: Laura likes the idea that the hero is brought down by their own weakness, and that tragedies explore intense things like power and jealousy.
The history plays also share common features:

items: There are 10 plays that focus on English history.
The central question seems to be: what makes a good monarch (king or queen)?

blocks.text: ‘Richard III’ is an example of a history play.

blocks.label: Jun’s idea
blocks.text: Jun says that because there are ten history plays, Shakespeare must have explored what it means to be a monarch in a lot of different ways.
The comedies have common features too:

items: They often focus on love and end in marriage.
The plot is **intricate** (complicated) and full of surprises.
There can be **slapstick humour**: physical comedy, sometimes violent but intended to make people laugh.

blocks.text: Shakespearean comedies usually focus on love, and end in marriage.
There is one more genre. **Tragicomedies** are plays which combine both tragic and comic elements.
Tragicomedy is not one of the genres in the First Folio. It is a genre that scholars added.

blocks.q: Who added tragicomedy to Shakespeare’s genres?
blocks.why: Tragicomedy was not included in the First Folio; it was added by scholars to describe plays that combine tragic and comic elements.

blocks.q: Put each feature under the genre it belongs to.

items.text: A hero who dies because of a weakness in themselves
Asks what makes a good monarch
One of 10 plays about English history
Often focuses on love and ends in marriage
An intricate plot full of surprises
Combines elements of tragedy and comedy

slides.title: Match the play to its genre

blocks.q: Match each play to its genre in the First Folio.

blocks.text: Look at the plot of ‘A Midsummer Night’s Dream’. How does it tell us that the play is a comedy?

items: Act 1: Hermia and Lysander run away from Athens.
Act 2: Lysander falls in love with Helena.
Act 3: Titania falls in love with Bottom (transformed into a donkey); Demetrius falls in love with Helena.
Act 4: the magical love potion is removed from Lysander and Titania.
Act 5: the Athenian nobles get married and then watch a play.

blocks.label: Comedy clue: love and marriage
blocks.text: The plot focuses on love, with people falling in and out of love, and it ends with marriages, such as Hermia and Lysander, and Helena and Demetrius.
In Act 3, Puck tells Oberon: “Titania waked and straightway loved an ass.” (3.2.34-42)

blocks.label: A moment of slapstick
blocks.text: A character becomes an ass. An ‘ass’ is a donkey, and also another word for a fool. This is physical comedy, a moment of slapstick.
Then Puck realises he has put the magical love potion on the wrong person: “This is the woman, but not this the man.”

blocks.label: A plot twist
blocks.text: The story becomes more intricate as misunderstandings build and build.
‘Macbeth’ is another Shakespearean play. Here is its plot:

items: Macbeth, an ambitious soldier, is told by three witches that he will become King of Scotland.
Macbeth kills the current King of Scotland and takes the throne.
Macbeth kills a number of people to hold onto his power; he sees the ghost of one of them.
Macbeth speaks to the witches again; the people of Scotland are very unhappy with how he rules them.
Macbeth is killed and a better king takes over Scotland.

blocks.label: What genre is it?
blocks.text: It is a tragedy. It explores ambition and power, and the hero dies. It does not focus on love and end in marriage like ‘A Midsummer Night’s Dream’.

blocks.q: Answer these questions about ‘A Midsummer Night’s Dream’.

items.q: Which is the best reason that the play is a comedy?
options: The hero dies because of a weakness
It focuses on love, has surprises and ends in marriages
It asks what makes a good monarch

items.q: Puck puts the love potion on the wrong person and the plot gets more complicated. Which key word describes this kind of plot?
Which key word means physical comedy, sometimes violent but intended to make people laugh?

blocks.label: Watch out!
blocks.text: A comedy can still have sad moments. When we decide on the genre, we look at the overall tone, plot and features of the play.

slides.title: Understanding the genre of ‘A Midsummer Night’s Dream’

items: The First Folio divides Shakespeare’s plays into tragedies, histories and comedies.
An additional genre, tragicomedies, has been used to describe plays which combine both tragic and comic elements.
Shakespearean comedies usually focus on love, and end in marriage.
The plots of comedies are often intricate and include a number of surprises and plot twists.
Shakespearean comedies often include slapstick humour.

flashcards.back:

Example: ‘A Midsummer Night’s Dream’.
A play that combines elements of both tragedy and comedy. It was not in the First Folio; scholars added the genre.

flashcards.back: Bottom’s head is turned into a donkey’s head (an ass) and Titania falls in love with him.

flashcards.back: Puck realises he has put the magical love potion on the wrong person.

flashcards.front: How does the ending of ‘A Midsummer Night’s Dream’ show it is a comedy?
flashcards.back: It ends with marriages: the Athenian nobles get married.

worksheet.title: Worksheet: Understanding the genre of William Shakespeare’s ‘A Midsummer Night’s Dream’
worksheet.instructions: Answer each question with a word, a number or a short phrase, using what you learned about Shakespeare’s genres.

questions.prompt: What is the name of the first collection of Shakespeare’s plays?
questions.explanation: The First Folio was published in 1623, seven years after Shakespeare’s death.

questions.prompt: In which year was the First Folio published?
questions.explanation: It was published in 1623, seven years after Shakespeare’s death.

questions.prompt: How many of Shakespeare’s plays does the First Folio contain?
questions.explanation: The First Folio contains 36 of Shakespeare’s plays.

questions.prompt: Which genre includes a hero who dies because of a weakness in themselves?
questions.explanation: Tragedies explore power, ambition and jealousy, with a hero brought down by their own weakness.

questions.prompt: How many history plays are there? (Write the number.)
questions.explanation: There are 10 plays that focus on English history.

questions.prompt: Which word means ‘complicated’ and describes the plots of comedies?
questions.explanation: Comedies often have intricate plots full of surprises.

questions.prompt: Which type of humour is physical comedy, sometimes violent but intended to make people laugh?
questions.explanation: That is the definition of slapstick humour.

questions.prompt: Which genre combines elements of both tragedy and comedy?
questions.explanation: Tragicomedies combine tragic and comic elements. Scholars added this genre; it is not in the First Folio.

questions.prompt: In the plot of ‘Macbeth’, an ambitious soldier is told by three witches he will be king and he is later killed. Which genre is ‘Macbeth’?
questions.explanation: It explores ambition and power and ends with the hero’s death, so it is a tragedy.
